extracted.intended_audience: patentees, patent agents, and patent examiners (Canada)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on Canadian post‑grant procedures: re‑examination (including second stage and certificates), reissue (requirements, evidence, filing and examination), and additional patent term (eligibility, calculation, process). Intended to direct applicants/agents and examiners how to prepare, evaluate, and decide such requests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Start of second-stage re-examination
rubrics_metrics.description: The re-examination based on a substantial new question of patentability begins upon a reply from the patentee or upon the expiration of three months from the notification from the board of a substantial new question of patentability (subsection 48.3(1) of the Patent Act).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If there has been no reply the board will, as a courtesy, send a letter indicating re-examination has begun and advise that absent further submissions a decision and certificate of re-examination will be issued under subsection 48.4(1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Board exchanges and preliminary opinions during re-examination
rubrics_metrics.description: During the re-examination proceeding there may be multiple exchanges; letters from the board will set out the board’s preliminary opinions on the patentability of claims subject to re-examination and any proposed amendments made by the patentee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Final determinations on patentability are reserved until issuance of a certificate of re-examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permissible amendments during re-examination
rubrics_metrics.description: The patentee may propose any amendment to the patent (including description and/or drawings) (subsection 48.3(2) of the Patent Act). Any amended or new claims proposed must be numbered consecutively beginning with the number immediately following the number of the last claim of the issued patent (section 123 of the Patent Rules).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All amendments must be proposed in accordance with the Patent Rules and numbered consecutively.

rubrics_metrics.name: No enlargement of claim scope in re-examination amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: No amendment or new claim shall enlarge the scope of a claim of the patent (subsection 48.3(2) of the Patent Act).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is taken to mean any proposed claim must, at a minimum, include all features of the broadest independent claim of the patent — a proposed claim may not broaden protection in some respects even if narrowed in others.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oral submissions in re-examination
rubrics_metrics.description: As part of exchanges during re-examination the patentee may make submissions orally and/or in writing; oral submissions may be conducted in person, via teleconference or videoconference, at the option of the patentee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patentees may choose the mode of oral presentation; both written and oral submissions form part of the record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time limit for second-stage re-examination completion
rubrics_metrics.description: Pursuant to subsection 48.3(3) of the Patent Act, the second stage of re-examination must be completed within twelve months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Board procedures and exchanges should be managed to meet the 12‑month statutory limit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal equivalence of re-examination determinations
rubrics_metrics.description: Determinations of a re-examination board are functionally equivalent to a decision of the Commissioner of Patents under section 40 of the Patent Act; they are a re-determination of validity of claims within the circumstances set out in sections 48.1 to 48.5.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The board must be satisfied the patentee is not 'by law' entitled to a claim to cancel it; the same criteria apply to decisions not to incorporate amendments, with the additional requirement that an amendment not enlarge the scope of a claim.

rubrics_metrics.name: Outcomes in certificate of re-examination
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon completion the re-examination board will issue a certificate of re-examination which may: cancel any claim determined unpatentable; confirm any claim determined patentable; or incorporate any proposed amended or new claim determined patentable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A decision letter outlining the reasons accompanies the certificate; registration certificate attaches the certificate to the patent and a new cover page is generated and stored in electronic files and the Canadian Patent Database.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of canceling an independent claim
rubrics_metrics.description: If a certificate indicates an independent claim is cancelled, this removes the scope of protection afforded by the claim but does not mean the text of the independent claim is no longer considered part of any dependent claim that refers to it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cancellation is a removal of scope, not necessarily textual deletion from dependent claim references.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retroactive and conditional effects of re-examination certificate
rubrics_metrics.description: Effects set out in subsection 48.4(3): (a) if some claims cancelled, patent deemed issued in corrected form from grant date; (b) if all claims cancelled, patent deemed never to have been issued; (c) amended or new claims effective from date of certificate for unexpired term.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Invalidity is retroactive, but addition/amendment of claims only gives rights for remaining term. Effects do not apply until appeal period expires, and if appealed only apply to extent reflected in final judicial judgment (subsection 48.4(4)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal from re-examination
rubrics_metrics.description: A decision of the re-examination board that accompanies a certificate may be appealed by the patentee to the Federal Court (subsection 48.5(1)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appeal must be taken within three months from the date a copy of the certificate is sent by registered mail to the patentee (subsection 48.5(2)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose and discretionary nature of reissue
rubrics_metrics.description: Reissue (section 47) is a mechanism to correct a 'defective or inoperative' patent, providing equitable relief for clear accident and mistake in drafting; the Commissioner 'may' grant a reissued patent but discretion is only exercisable when subsection 47(1) conditions are met.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications outside the statute must be refused; exercise of discretion must be compatible with the purpose of the provision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time limit to file reissue application
rubrics_metrics.description: Subsection 47(1) requires a patent be surrendered within four years from its date of grant to obtain a reissue — interpreted as filing the application for reissue within four years from the grant of the original patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Surrender of the original patent is considered to occur on submission of the application for reissue (Form 1), but only takes effect if a new patent is issued. The original patent should never be returned to the Office for reissue purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds for 'defective or inoperative' patent
rubrics_metrics.description: Pursuant to subsection 47(1) a patent is 'defective or inoperative' where, due to some error, the original patent failed to fulfil the applicant’s intent upon grant. Two primary reasons: (1) insufficient description and specification; and (2) the patentee having claimed more or less than they had a right to claim as new.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This relates to scope of protection or quality of description; does not equate to defects in compliance with the Act and Rules for validity purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reissue not available for judicially invalid or lapsed patents
rubrics_metrics.description: The words 'defective or inoperative' do not encompass reissue of a patent judicially declared invalid or a patent for which all rights have lapsed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reissue is not a substitute for reopening prosecution; it must meet subsection 47(1) requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nature of the error and applicant's intent for reissue
rubrics_metrics.description: Error must have 'arisen from inadvertence, accident or mistake, without any fraudulent or deceptive intention' and must have resulted in a patent that fails to express the applicant's intended invention as of the date of issuance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mere support in the original patent for proposed amendments is insufficient; the patentee must show evidence of what the applicant intended. Evidence must generally pre-date issuance; onus lies with patentee; presumption is that intent was fulfilled unless rebutted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permissible evidence to establish reissue error
rubrics_metrics.description: Evidence considered as a whole can include the text of the patent, actions taken during prosecution of the original application, corresponding applications in other jurisdictions and communications indicating intended actions that were never taken.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To be of practical use, the evidence must pre-date issuance; mere allegation is not evidence; extent of applicant/patent agent experience may be considered; error could be caused by anyone during prosecution but intent must be that of the applicant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Insufficient description and specification indicators
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent defective for insufficient description/specification lacks textual/graphical matter or includes wrong matter contrary to inventor intent, e.g., failure to accurately claim or describe the invention, claim subcombinations, include dependent claims, or claims to different categories of invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such failings could indicate reissue is appropriate if they show the patent does not express applicant intent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claiming more or less than entitled
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent is defective for claiming more or less when the claims protect more or less subject-matter than the patentee intended; errors in description/drawings can cause this defect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reissue may be appropriate to correct scope mismatches if they meet subsection 47(1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Same invention requirement for reissue
rubrics_metrics.description: Any amended description/specification in reissue must be directed to the 'same invention ... for which the original patent was granted' (subsection 47(1)). All matter in a reissued patent must find support somewhere in the original patent's description, drawings or claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No requirement for identical inventive concept; matter inferable from original description/drawings/claims or admitted prior art is acceptable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application content and consistency for reissue
rubrics_metrics.description: An application for reissue must include Form 1 of Schedule 1 completed per instructions (section 118 of the Patent Rules) and must include an amended description, drawings and/or claims. All changes must be consistent with defects identified in Form 1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patentee should submit the most relevant available evidence; the original patent should never be returned to the Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form 1 requirements and sections
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 3 of Form 1 must identify specifically how the patent is defective/inoperative; Section 4 must illustrate how the error arose and refer to submitted evidence; Section 5 details when/how the patentee became aware of the error (error must have been discovered after patent was issued).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 4 should link to applicable evidence; Section 5 circumstances may affect determination of whether applicant's intent was unfulfilled. Form 1 may not be amended (see examination guidance).

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination and verification of reissue applications
rubrics_metrics.description: The Reissue Board first verifies compliance with section 47 (as detailed in sections 31.01.02–31.01.05); if compliant, an examiner of the relevant art verifies the reissued patent would comply with the rest of the Patent Act and Rules (analogous to examination of a patent application).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If noncompliant an office letter is issued; patentee may respond with argument, evidence and/or amendments (but Form 1 cannot be amended); impasses may be referred to Patent Appeal Board and ultimately Commissioner. Present best evidence at filing; application does not go abandoned for failure to respond and no reinstatement fees apply; patentee may withdraw application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form 1 immutability
rubrics_metrics.description: Form 1 may not be amended; section 47 does not permit amendments to Form 1 that change the reasons for reissue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All issues and evidence should be before the Reissue Board and examiner prior to any referral to the Patent Appeal Board; patentee should present best evidence at filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple applications for reissue and co-existence
rubrics_metrics.description: A patentee may file separate applications for reissue in respect of distinct parts of the invention covered by the original patent (subsection 47(3)); each must be filed within four years of original grant. Each separate application must be independently patentable to ensure double patenting does not arise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commissioner will not call for division of an application for reissue; where multiple co-existing applications do not cover separate parts only one reissued patent (at most) can be granted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling subject-matter from refused co-existing reissue applications
rubrics_metrics.description: If one or more co-existing applications for reissue are compliant but at least one is refused or withdrawn, the patentee may, before expiry of a specified time, introduce subject-matter from the refused/withdrawn application into a compliant one provided that subject-matter appeared in the original patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If introduced matter causes noncompliance, examination continues until compliant/refused/withdrawn; if no response within specified time, patents proceed based on compliant applications on file.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reissue of a reissued patent
rubrics_metrics.description: A reissued patent may itself be reissued provided the application is filed within four years of the date of grant of the original patent (not of the reissued patent) and the invention sought is directed to the same invention for which the original patent was granted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timing must reference the original patent grant date for the four‑year limit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retroactive effect and maintenance fees for reissued patent
rubrics_metrics.description: Effect of reissue is retroactive and rights exist with respect to the reissued patent as if they had been in effect as of the original grant date (subsection 47(2)). No additional maintenance fees apply to an application for reissue; maintenance fees remain payable on the original patent until it reissues, then on the reissued patent under the same due dates as the original patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A reissued patent may not be withdrawn after it has been issued in favour of the original patent. Pending actions unaffected to the extent their claims are identical in scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal from refusal to grant reissue
rubrics_metrics.description: Although not explicitly provided in the Patent Act, a refusal to grant a reissue by the Commissioner is subject to appeal to the Federal Court under section 41 of the Patent Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patentees should be aware of judicial remedy where refusal occurs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose and scope of additional term
rubrics_metrics.description: An additional term may be granted to compensate patentees for unreasonable delays in processing patent applications; it begins on expiry of the 20‑year standard term of an eligible patent, provided the patent remains valid until expiry of the standard term.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Additional term is distinct from certificates of supplementary protection (CSP) and may run concurrently with a CSP if both are granted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility: filing date and Later Date requirement for additional term
rubrics_metrics.description: An additional term is only applicable for patents if the application was filed on or after December 1, 2020. The patent must have been issued after the Later Date — the later of: (i) the third anniversary of the date of the request for examination, and (ii) the fifth anniversary of the patent's applicable day (national entry date for PCT national phase, presentation date for divisional, or filing date for any other application) (paragraphs 46.1(1)(a)–(c)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If these date-based eligibility criteria are not met the application is dismissed (deemed never to have been made).

rubrics_metrics.name: Calculation examples for the Later Date
rubrics_metrics.description: Examples illustrating how the Later Date is calculated for PCT national entry, divisional, and other applications: the Later Date is the later of five years from the applicable day and three years from the request for examination date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples show calendar calculations to determine the Later Date used in additional term computation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application timing and fee for additional term
rubrics_metrics.description: Patentee must submit a compliant application for additional term and pay the fee within three months after the issue date of the patent (subsection 117.01(1), (3) of the Patent Rules); the application must be in writing and indicate the applicable patent number (paragraph 46.1(1)(c)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An error in the patent number may be corrected before the later of three months after issue and one month after application receipt (subsection 117.01(2)). Only one application per patent may be submitted, but a dismissed (ineligible) application is deemed never made and the patentee may apply again.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dismissal for ineligibility of additional term application
rubrics_metrics.description: If eligibility criteria under paragraphs 46.1(1)(a)–(c) are not met, the application for additional term is dismissed and deemed never to have been made; the Commissioner will send notice (subsection 117.01(5)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A dismissed application does not count as having been made; patentee may reapply if appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preliminary determination and observations for additional term
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commissioner will send a Notice of Preliminary Determination of the duration of additional term (subsection 117.01(6)); the patentee has two months from that notice to provide observations (subsection 117.01(7)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Observations will be considered before the Commissioner issues a certificate or dismissal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Issuance of additional term certificate or dismissal
rubrics_metrics.description: After observations, the Commissioner will issue either a certificate of additional term specifying number of days granted (subsection 46.1(7)) or a dismissal if duration is determined to be zero days or less (subsection 46.1(5)). Reasons will be provided (subsection 117.01(8)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The certificate will include filing date, title, and issue day and will be available on the CIPO website; Commissioner may correct typographical errors (subsection 117.04).

rubrics_metrics.name: Calculation of duration of additional term
rubrics_metrics.description: Duration is the number of days between the Later Date (excluded) and the issue date of the patent (included) less the number of days to be subtracted under the Patent Rules (subsection 46.1(4), section 117.03).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example provided: Later Date Jan 20, 2026; issue date Jul 14, 2026 -> 175 days before subtraction of applicable days.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and rules for subtracted days in additional term calculation
rubrics_metrics.description: Subtracted days are the total number of days within all applicable periods determined under section 117.03 of the Patent Rules; there may be multiple applicable periods, periods may overlap, but a calendar day may be subtracted only once.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Counting rules: include the first day, exclude the last day; if the period ends on or before it begins the number is zero; if a period does not end before issuance it ends on date of issuance. Specific types of periods (e.g., prior to request for examination, abandonment, extensions) are enumerated in section 117.03.

rubrics_metrics.name: General rules for applicable periods of time
rubrics_metrics.description: Subsection 117.03(1) defines periods reflecting events during application history; any given period may apply more than once; overlapping periods count each day only once; certain pre‑request periods may be excluded depending on which event defines the Later Date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Periods include times from applicable day to compliant request for examination or abandonment, times when application is deemed abandoned, extension periods, and notice periods; the specific paragraphs of 117.03 govern inclusion/exclusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Period rules for notices affecting additional term
rubrics_metrics.description: If a notice is sent requiring action, days in the applicable period beginning on the date of the notice will be subtracted; depending on notice type the period ends on a specified day or earlier of two days (e.g., action taken or abandonment).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In most cases the period begins on the date of the notice; the handling depends on the notice type and its deadlines as defined in the Rules.
